3.8   S08: Continuity when singular references or positive residuals degenerate
Status: unresolved question in the manuscript.
Full problem description. Give geometric or singularity conditions on varying admissible
references φj and backgrounds that imply convergence of Bφj on continuous tests and place all
cluster supports in Aφ (F ) for the limiting reference. Include degenerate residual forms and arbitrary
singularities.
State of the art. A genuine smaller-background envelope tending to reference zero gives uniform
convergence of scalar functionals and uniformly integrable supports. Relative comparison of positive
divisorial residuals gives a geometric criterion. Entropy estimates yield compactness while references
vary. BMP model-volume and ﬁxed-divisor regimes supply additional equation stability.
Remaining gap. Identify the limiting functional when residual positivity fails or singularities
cease to be divisorial. Compactness of measures alone does not identify their supporting func-
tional. State assumptions ensuring the limiting reference is in a solvable regime rather than silently
assuming existence there.
Source location.     book/author/section_reference_comparison.tex:45; book/author/
section_prescribed_dual_entropy.tex:38.

unchanged_original_condition_task.problem: Let X be a connected compact complex n-fold, n>=2, with a smooth positive probability volume dV and dd^c=(i/(2 pi))partial barpartial. All potentials are genuine canonical upper representatives. For a smooth semipositive big real (1,1) background theta, define P_theta(f) as the usc envelope of genuine theta-psh v<=f (equivalently the a.e. obstacle convention with canonical regularization). Put u preceq phi when u<=phi+C, and u~phi for mutual bounded difference including common poles. Define P_theta[phi]=(lim_{C->infinity}P_theta(min(phi+C,0)))^*. An ordinary model reference is sup phi=0 and P_theta[phi]=phi. The standard admissible reference regime additionally requires a genuine envelope P_(epsilon theta)(phi) for some 0<epsilon<1. Then each bounded logarithmic density F has an ordinary-type solution MA_ext_theta(u)=c_phi(F)exp(F)dV with u~phi and scalar c_phi(F)>0 uniquely determined; potential uniqueness is not automatic. Set B_phi(F)=log c_phi(F). For F continuous define A_phi(F) as all Borel probabilities nu such that B_phi(G)<=B_phi(F)-integral(G-F)dnu for every G continuous. In the admissible regime B_phi is concave, decreasing, 1-Lipschitz, and B_phi(F+a)=B_phi(F)-a; A_phi(F) is nonempty compact convex and absolutely continuous with respect to dV. Generic singleton supports hold on a dense G_delta. The same bounded-type functional exists for arbitrary Hermitian theta and phi=0. Smooth strictly positive solution forms Omega=theta+dd^c u have the classical adjoint: a positive smooth weight rho with dd^c(rho Omega^(n-1))=0 and nu=rho Omega^n/integral rho Omega^n. Extended products for rough potentials are non-pluripolar products with the smooth-background corrections; a weighted product is not declared defined merely because a supporting probability exists. Original S08 asks for geometric or singularity conditions on varying admissible references phi_j and backgrounds theta_j giving convergence of their B_(theta_j,phi_j) on continuous tests, and identifying every cluster supporting probability as an element of A_(theta,phi)(F) at the limiting data. Include degenerate residual forms and singularities beyond divisorial ones. Specify the limiting type and prove that the limit is in a solvable regime, rather than assuming the equation one intends to establish. Known facts: for fixed theta, a genuine smaller-background envelope P_(epsilon_j theta)(phi_j) with epsilon_j->0 implies uniform B_phi_j->B_0, with uniformly integrable support densities and correct cluster identification. More generally uniform functional distance Delta(phi_j,phi)=sup_{G continuous}|B_phi_j(G)-B_phi(G)|->0 gives the support stability, but assuming this desired functional convergence does not supply a geometric criterion. Relative two-sided comparison of strictly positive backgrounds gives uniform functional comparison, and positive divisorial residuals have such criteria. Entropy bounds give compactness while references vary; BMP model-volume and fixed-divisor cases provide further equation stability. These established mechanisms do not identify a limiting functional once residual positivity fails or singularities cease to be divisorial. Compactness of probabilities alone is not cluster identification. No candidate geometric/singularity hypothesis or proof is supplied.
unchanged_original_condition_task.completionCriteria: Prove new explicit geometric or singularity sufficient conditions covering a genuinely degenerate residual or nondivisorial reference regime, with an actual nontrivial family, existence of the limiting functional and its solvable reference class, convergence on continuous tests and correct identification of all cluster supports. Do not assume the desired B convergence as the condition itself or silently assume limiting solvability. State the reference/type, background, density and approximation normalizations, quantitative estimates and topology. Independently reconstruct the argument and check exact indispensable premises at primary sources. A restricted result must stay scoped and cannot close every arbitrary-singularity degeneration.

exact_primary_application_assessment: The official DDL v3 TheoremA(i) bounded ordinary-type conclusion was reread at text103-145. The article proves compact connected Kahler X, closed big theta, an actual positive-mass ordinary model, a genuine smaller-background witness and a matching L-infinity density relative to an auxiliary Kahler volume before invoking it. The operator/background/measure scale factors2pi and(2pi)^n are explicit. Reuse the unchanged previously root-assessed complete exact primary convex, canonical extension/envelope, bounded BT/CLN/difference, non-pluripolar and blowup proofs (46 historical page views). Task quotations remain excluded as external evidence. No residual strict positivity, arbitrary equation existence or desired functional convergence is assumed.
mathematical_application_assessment: The common translated simplex gives actual canonical reference models, an admissibility witness and positive limiting mass. Angular differentiation fixes n!Vol(P). The common inscribed ball controls volume ratios under Hausdorff convergence, so the functional convergence follows from geometry. The curved square-root body has nonanalytic isolated poles and varying ordinary types. The second resolved residual is rank1 on E_q, with positive mass1-t^n for0<t<1; t1 zero mass is explicitly excluded for every bounded residual, rather than silently treated as solvable.

clause_assessment.requested: Geometric or singularity hypotheses on varying references/backgrounds
clause_assessment.proved: Hausdorff-converging convex bodies with a common translated simplex, positive converging background scales and a fixed point blowup supply explicit hypotheses, independent of the desired B convergence.

clause_assessment.requested: A genuinely nondivisorial or degenerate residual regime
clause_assessment.proved: Square-root convex bodies give isolated genuinely nonanalytic poles with varying ordinary types. The disjoint-center resolution gives smooth residuals of exact rank1 on an exceptional divisor and positive top mass.

clause_assessment.requested: Establish the limiting admissible solvable type
clause_assessment.proved: An explicit entropy-conjugate envelope and smaller-background logarithmic witness establish the ordinary model at the limit. Computed positive mass and exact DDL hypotheses then give every bounded-density ordinary-type equation.

clause_assessment.requested: Convergence of normalization functionals on continuous tests
clause_assessment.proved: B_j(G)=log(r_j^n n!Vol(P_j))-log integral exp(G)dV; a uniform-in-G Hausdorff/scaling error bound is proved from the common simplex geometry.

Every support is exactly exp(F)dV/Z(F) by Jensen and two-sided differentiation. Uniform F_j convergence gives the explicit total-variation bound, hence every cluster belongs to the limiting supporting set.
Background smooth convergence, reference L1 and local-uniform convergence, the original operator coefficient, positive nonanalytic endpoint and excluded analytic zero-mass endpoint are all checked.

scope_assessment: The original condition-finding question is answered by an explicit family covering both requested new regimes, with independent limiting solvability and all support-cluster identities. This does not assert stability for arbitrary Hermitian torsion, every singularity or moving modifications. The original sufficient-condition task and the larger unresolved programme retain distinct scopes.
